result.topic_en: This page summarizes the integrals of dx/(a+bx+cxx)+dy/(a+by+cyy)=0 and dx/√(A+Bx+Cxx)−dy/√(A+By+Cyy)=0 under the condition that x=k when y=0, giving three equivalent forms of the first integral and an algebraic form of the second.
result.transcription:

Theorema II.
§. 49. Si haec aequatio differentialis:
$\frac{dx}{a+bx+cxx} + \frac{dy}{a+by+cyy} = 0$
ita integretur, vt poſito $y=0$ fiat $x=k$, integrale ſupra triplici modo eſt inuentum; erit enim:
I. $\frac{b+c(x+y)}{cxy-a} = -\frac{b+ck}{a}$;
II. $\frac{a(x+y)+bxy}{cxy-a} = -k$
III. $\frac{b+c(x+y)}{a(x+y)+bxy} = \frac{b+ck}{ak}$.
Theorema III.
§. 50. Si haec aequatio differentialis:
$\frac{dx}{\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cxx)}} - \frac{dy}{\sqrt{(A+By+Cyy)}} = 0$
ita integretur, vt poſito $y=0$ fiat $x=k$, integrale erit
$-B(x+y) - 2Cxy + 2\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cxx)}\sqrt{(A+By+Cyy)} =$
$-Bk + 2\sqrt{A(A+Bk+Ckk)}$, ſiue
$B(k-x-y) - 2Cxy = 2\sqrt{A(A+Bk+Ckk)}$
$-2\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cxx)(A+By+Cyy)}$
Corollarium.
§. 51. Hinc ergo patet, ſi aequatio differentialis propoſita, fuerit iſta:
$\frac{dx}{\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cxx)}} = \frac{dy}{\sqrt{(A+By+Cyy)}} = 0$,
eaque integretur ita, vt poſito $y=0$ fiat $x=k$, integrale fore
$B(k-x-y) - 2Cxy = 2\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cxx)}$
$\sqrt{(A+By+Cyy)} - 2\sqrt{A(A+Bk+Ckk)}$.
